committees.name: Joint Standing Committee on Migration
committees.why: Can inquire into migration and put offshore partner-visa delays on the parliamentary record. Includes government, opposition, Greens and an independent — not only ministers.

committees.name: Senate Legal and Constitutional Affairs Legislation Committee
committees.why: This committee questions Home Affairs at Senate estimates. Any senator may attend; these six sit on it.

pillars.title: 1. Parliament
pillars.blurb: Your MP, the migration committee, and senators. This is the path that most often produces a real departmental enquiry. Use the tabs above. Opposition and crossbench count.

pillars.title: 2. Watchdogs
pillars.blurb: A rights or delay complaint is a record. Your MP is the enquiry. The Commission and Ombudsman do not grant 309s and rarely shorten the queue.

links.title: Commonwealth Ombudsman
links.blurb: Complaint about Home Affairs delay or process. Not a grant, not a queue jump.
links.label: Ombudsman

links.title: Australian Human Rights Commission
links.blurb: Family-life complaint about Commonwealth action. Slow. Unlikely to move your file. Use measured language — ‘engages family life’, not ‘violation’.
links.label: AHRC complaints

pillars.note: Courts do not run the 309 queue. Do not file from this site. A registered lawyer is the only person to ask about unreasonable delay.

pillars.title: 3. Community
pillars.blurb: Peak bodies can amplify many similar stories. They will not casework your application.

links.title: FECCA
links.blurb: Federation of Ethnic Communities' Councils — national multicultural voice.
links.label: fecca.org.au

links.title: Migration Institute of Australia
links.blurb: Professionals' body. Policy submissions, not a free agent for your file.
links.label: mia.org.au

links.title: Find a registered migration agent
links.blurb: MARA register — paid advice if you need it. This site is not immigration assistance.
links.label: MARA find an agent

pillars.title: 4. Media
pillars.blurb: One local or national desk, facts, your suburb, no pile-on. A journalist is not your caseworker. Never send visa documents unasked.

links.title: SBS News
links.blurb: Often covers migrant families and non-English speaking audiences.
links.label: SBS contact

pillars.note: Pitch in six lines: who you are, suburb, 309 wait, Direction 117, what you want understood (home, living together, strain). Offer to talk. Do not attach passports.

support.blurb: If the wait is affecting your safety or you need to talk: Lifeline 13 11 14.
support.label: Lifeline
